analysis:
## Technical analysis (Tuesday June 30 — Q2 2026 close)

**BTC Q2 2026 late-session price: ~$58,592 (−2.76% from June 29 $60,252.62).** Crypto.com MCP (21:47 UTC): O$60,255.20 / H$60,593.04 / L$58,186.01 / C$58,591.96. Volume 3,760 BTC ($221.3M). Final midnight UTC close pending; price trend is established.

**Trend: Bearish.** Ten consecutive UTC closes below the $62,000 re-entry gate. The distribution close sequence since June 24 exit: $61,078 → $59,795 → $60,103 → $60,024 → $59,578 → $60,253 → ~$58,592. The June 29 bounce to $60,253 (best close of the distribution window, on the best US macro session of the correction cycle) has already reversed — June 30 closed below the June 28 close ($59,578). Classic dead-cat bounce confirmation.

**Momentum: Bearish.** RSI estimated below 30 — approaching oversold territory. Fear & Greed in Extreme Fear zone throughout the distribution window. Historically, Extreme Fear precedes medium-term recoveries in post-halving cycles, but this is a mean-reversion signal, not an immediate entry trigger. The IBIT inflow resumption condition must activate first.

**Volume: Distribution, not capitulation.** June 30 volume 3,760 BTC ($221.3M) — above recent low-volume sessions (June 27: 1,466 BTC; June 28: 2,096 BTC) but consistent with June 29 distribution session (3,433 BTC). Volume is elevated on the downside. Capitulation bottoms typically show a sharp volume spike (2-3× average) with an intraday V-reversal; today shows consistent selling without a volume exhaustion spike — distribution, not capitulation.

**★ Strongest resistance: $62,000** — the re-entry gate. Ten consecutive UTC closes locked below this level since the June 24 exit. Every rally in the distribution window (June 29 high $60,784; June 27 high $60,948; June 26 high $60,767) has stalled well below $62,000. The two-consecutive-midnight-UTC-close requirement means even a single intraday spike above $62,000 is insufficient. At $58,592, $62,000 is +5.82% away. The $4.06B in June IBIT outflows confirm institutional sellers are positioned to sell into any $62,000 approach.

**★ Strongest support: $58,100** — the structural accumulation zone from April 2026. The June 30 session low of $58,186 was only $86 above this level. This support has been approached three times in the distribution window (June 26 low $58,325; June 29 low $58,884; June 30 low $58,186 is the closest approach yet). A confirmed UTC close below $58,100 would represent a new multi-month low and activate $57,500 as the next structural target.

**Pattern: Dead-cat bounce confirmed.** The June 29 rally to $60,253 — on the SCOTUS ruling, GOOGL first Dow day, and Nasdaq +2.07%, the best US macro session of the 2026 correction cycle — was the dead-cat bounce. June 30 followed with a -2.76% decline to new lows. The strongest catalyst available failed to produce a sustained recovery; the distribution pattern continued immediately after. The $62,000 gate is structural.

**Volume confirms distribution.** Today's elevated volume (3,760 BTC) on a new closing low confirms sellers are not exhausted. The bull case would require a session where volume spikes on an upday AND IBIT shows net inflows — neither condition is present.

**Decision point: $58,100.** Either BTC holds this level (stabilization → watch for IBIT inflow recovery and gate approach) or breaks it (next structural test $57,500, potentially deepening the correction). The July 1 UTC session is the first critical test.

so_what.line: BTC closes Q2 2026 at ~$58,592 — down 2.76% on the day the S&P 500 posted its best quarter in six years; ten consecutive closes below the $62,000 re-entry gate and record IBIT outflows ($4.06B in June) leave the framework unchanged: flat/cash until the gate plus inflows plus NFP all confirm.
so_what.bull: US equity regime gates just cleared for the first time since May 14 (SPX > 7,460), IBIT outflows are decelerating from $692M to $300M, and Extreme Fear readings at these levels have historically preceded 15-30% recoveries in post-halving cycles — the setup for re-entry above $62,000 is building even if the trigger hasn't fired.
so_what.bear: Ten consecutive closes below the re-entry gate, a lower-high and lower-low on the best US equity quarter in six years, and record June IBIT outflows ($4.06B) — the distribution ceiling at $62,000 is structural and the $58,100 structural support was just $86 above the session low.
